findings: All four existing implementation bodies are byte-for-byte unchanged after removing include directives; the new behavior is header availability and missing constant definitions.
The memfd flags, namespace ioctl/type magic, fcntl seal operations and four x86_64 syscall numbers match the six supplied actual Bionic UAPI source files and the F_LINUX_SPECIFIC_BASE value.

Missing declarations are guarded with ifndef; existing declarations are checked by static_assert. The syscall fallback is limited to x86_64 without ILP32, so the LP64 numbers are not injected into x32 or another architecture.

The compatibility header uses the actual compiler/sysroot includes and conditional availability, without importing a different host UAPI tree. It does not add a successful fallback for a rejected syscall or weaken a runtime identity/capability check.
not_performed: No compiler, test binary, namespace, Android runtime, kernel syscall or Hepta operation was executed for this review.
The complete original four implementation files were not re-reviewed as runtime algorithms; this review confirms their include-only delta.
The five complete translation-unit matching compile and full engine build remain separate actual gates.
scope: complete 3979-byte portability patch and 2072-byte new header; include-only identity verification in four existing private C++ implementation files
